newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan sees no immediate cut in vegoil duty.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan sees no immediate cut in vegoil duty.

text.p: Pakistan has no immediate plans to cut duty on the import of vegetable oils as rumoured at the weekend, an official of the state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) said on Tuesday.
"There have been no cuts nor we have received any signal from the government about any proposed cuts in the near future," said the official, who asked not to be named.
Some dealers said at the weekend that import duty might be slashed by 1,000 rupees ($24.86) per tonne.
A dealer at Jaleel Brothers Ltd, who had earlier predicted a duty reduction, said on Tuesday this now seemed less likely.
"The market was expecting a cut, but apparently the government is not interested," he said.
Vegoil imports fell 5.39 percent to 56,477 tonnes in January from 59,696 tonnes in December.
